exceptions.rationale: Neon Auth 0.4.2-beta pins Better Auth 1.4.18 for client, cookie, and type adapters. The affected OIDC-provider, MCP-provider, organization, magic-link, and email-OTP server plugins are not instantiated through this adapter; the app's own agent-auth server uses Better Auth 1.6.26. Replacing Neon's exact pin is prohibited until Neon publishes a compatible release.

Patched Undici 7.29 is pinned for sandbox and jsdom, and Vercel Blob resolves patched 6.28. The remaining vulnerable 5.29 runtime branch belongs to the ConnectRPC v1 client for an operator-configured Life gateway; no patched 5.x release exists. Migrating it requires tested ConnectRPC v2 and Protobuf regeneration. Caller-controlled proxy, cookie, WebSocket, and destination configuration are not exposed, but HTTP parsing and denial-of-service residual risk remains until that migration.
Patched 4.x is direct. The residual 3.x/4.1 copies are build/content dependencies receiving repository-controlled Markdown frontmatter and schemas, not user-submitted YAML.
Fumadocs uses this during documentation builds over repository-controlled assets; no production upload/parser path calls it.
This is reachable only from the development-only Evalite CLI; the deployed Next.js service does not import or expose its static server.

The remaining 1.19 branch is used only by the AI SDK Devtools CLI. The deployed Next.js service does not start this server, and the advisory requires its Windows static-file path handling. The separate runtime MCP branch resolves patched 2.1.
The residual copy belongs to Neon Auth UI's Triplit dependency. Application code does not invoke the vulnerable negative-size non-secure generator.
The vulnerable copy is a Drizzle development-tool dependency. No esbuild development server is exposed in production.
The vulnerable parser is a development-only Evalite dependency and does not process production uploads; uploads are disabled pending private storage.
